deck: NEBLI::UC02::P3::Bio celular e tecidual::Histologia dos órgãos linfáticos

cards.text: The {{c1::primary}} lymphoid organs (bone marrow, thymus) make and educate lymphocytes; the {{c2::secondary}} ones (lymph node, spleen, MALT) are where the response happens.
Any molecule recognized as foreign and able to trigger the immune response is an {{c1::antigen}}.
cards.extra: Core job: tell self from non-self.

cards.text: The activated B lymphocyte does not secrete antibody directly: it becomes a {{c1::plasma cell}}, which secretes the antibody.
cards.extra: Resting B carries surface IgM/IgD as its antigen antenna.

cards.text: The surface marker of the T lymphocyte (cell-mediated response, cell-to-cell contact) is the {{c1::TCR}}.
Which T cell kills infected/tumor cells with {{c1::perforin}}? {{c2::Cytotoxic (CD8) T cell}}
Which T cell coordinates the response by secreting {{c1::interleukins}}? {{c2::Helper (CD4) T cell}}
Which T cell suppresses the response and prevents autoimmunity? {{c1::Regulatory T cell (Treg)}}
Which lymphocyte belongs to {{c1::innate}} immunity, killing abnormal cells with no prior sensitization, no TCR, and no memory? {{c2::NK cell}}
The macrophage not only phagocytoses: it breaks down the antigen and {{c1::presents}} it on its surface for the T cell.
cards.extra: Bridge from engulfing to the specific response.

cards.text: In lymphoid tissue, the fixed {{c1::reticular cell}} produces the {{c2::reticular fiber}} (type III collagen) that forms the scaffold.
cards.extra: Cell makes it; fiber is the product. Fixed macrophage = histiocyte.

cards.text: Rule in every lymphoid organ: the {{c1::fixed}} cells build the structure and filter; the {{c2::free}} cells (lymphocytes, plasma cells) run the response.
The lymphatic {{c1::nodule}} is a temporary, capsule-less structure needing antigenic stimulus; its {{c2::germinal center}} is a site of B-cell proliferation.
cards.extra: Germinal center = tissue reacting. No T cells made there.

cards.text: Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue is {{c1::MALT}}; in the gut it forms the {{c2::Peyer's patches}}.
The {{c1::B}} lymphocyte matures in the bone marrow; the {{c2::T}} lymphocyte is educated in the thymus.
In the thymus the {{c1::cortex}} is outer, dark, dense with immature thymocytes; the {{c2::medulla}} is inner and paler.
cards.extra: Lobules are incomplete, so neighboring medullae communicate.

cards.text: The thymic scaffold is made of {{c1::epithelial reticular cells}} (epithelial origin, joined by desmosomes), not ordinary reticular cells.
cards.extra: Scaffold of cells, not collagen fibers. They secrete thymosins.

cards.text: The blood-thymus barrier, isolating immature thymocytes from blood antigens, exists only in the thymic {{c1::cortex}}.
cards.extra: Medulla is not isolated; mature T waits there to enter circulation.

cards.text: Which acidophilic whorl of degenerated epithelial reticular cells is the histologic signature of the thymic medulla? {{c1::Hassall's corpuscle}}
cards.extra: No B cells, no germinal center. See Hassall = thymus.

cards.text: The thymus does not grow with age; it {{c1::involutes}}, peaking near puberty then replaced by fat.
Which lymphoid organ filters {{c1::lymph}} (not blood) via many afferent vessels in and one efferent vessel out at the hilum? {{c2::Lymph node}}
cards.extra: Many in, one out; concentrates filtered lymph.

cards.text: In the lymph node cortex sit the {{c1::B}}-cell nodules; in the paracortex (thymus-dependent area) sit the {{c2::T}} cells.
cards.extra: Medullary cords are rich in plasma cells.

cards.text: Lymphocytes enter the node from the {{c1::blood}}, crossing the paracortical {{c2::high endothelial venules}}, not via the afferent lymph.
Which clear space just under the capsule is the histologic signature of the lymph node, absent in the spleen? {{c1::Subcapsular sinus}}
Which lymphoid organ filters {{c1::blood}} and therefore has no afferent {{c2::lymphatic}} vessels? {{c3::Spleen}}
cards.extra: Blood enters via splenic artery → central artery.

cards.text: The splenic white pulp around the central artery is the {{c1::PALS}} (T-cell sheath) plus the B-cell {{c2::nodules}}.
cards.extra: Same pattern as the node: T around the vessel, B in nodules.

cards.text: The splenic red pulp is the blood compartment: {{c1::cords of Billroth}} (macrophage mesh) and {{c2::sinusoid}} capillaries, where old RBCs are culled.
In the spleen's {{c1::open}} circulation, blood is dumped into the cord and must squeeze back into the sinusoid; a stiff old RBC is trapped and {{c2::phagocytosed}}.
cards.extra: The structure IS the RBC quality-control mechanism.

cards.text: Which signature has an artery running inside the lymphoid tissue, unique to the spleen? {{c1::Nodule with a central artery}}
cards.extra: Reading triad: Hassall = thymus; subcapsular sinus = node; central artery = spleen.

cards.text: After splenectomy, the patient is dangerously vulnerable to {{c1::encapsulated bacteria}}, risking fulminant sepsis.
cards.extra: No splenic filter or red-pulp macrophages to catch them.
